Mega-Masters Explained: How Trump's Immigration Courts are Manufacturing Deportations

austinkocher.substack.com/p/mega-maste...
Watch or listen to my full conversation with the DU Courtwatch team, and read the recap, at austinkocher.substack.com.

Jenni came to this work through her own family's years in the system. Her advice is the simplest thing any of us can do. Go bear witness. Even if you don't follow all the legal jargon, sitting in a courtroom will teach you a lot.
Jasmine grew up in Aurora. She describes how thin the line in that courtroom is, where the only real difference between her and the person in custody can come down to a uniform.

The GEO-run facility covers its skylights with a painted image of the sky and lines its walls with awards and value words like accountability and character. It advertises its own decency while keeping what happens inside almost entirely out of view.
Ella put the reason for the whole project in one line. "The immigration court system as we know it today only exists because of a complete lack of transparency."

The DU Court Transparency Project is led by Rebecca Galemba, with Ella Iveslätt, Jasmine Salgado Simental, and Jenni Gutierrez Marquez. They sit in the gallery, take everything down by hand because no phones or laptops get past the door, and turn it into a public record.

Detained immigration court is the black box of the whole system. Hearings are civil proceedings, but they take place inside an ICE facility where few people have access. I sat down with the University of Denver team that documents one of those courtrooms in Aurora.

ICYMI: at the current pace, ICE will have booked over 800,000 people into detention by year's end and close to 1.75 million by the end of the term. Most people released from detention are now deported. See the graphs.
